purpose: Audit native Key-Control processing against the actual shipped PLOAM ISR, rather than infer behavior only from the deferred key state machine.

verification.cases: Slots1/2, new-key request followed by confirmation for each slot. All four complete40-byte reports and final downstream validity, upstream AES control and key selection match.
verification.scope: Actual stock key ISR, key generation, key validity/switch setters and report sender versus native key IRQ. Synthetic ONU-ID/KEK/RNG, real OpenSSL AES/CMAC. MMIO, packet consumption, queues, locks and ACK cryptography modeled; no software tasklet/FSM or optical execution.
verification.compiler: Host C compiler with real OpenSSL AES-128-ECB/CMAC; no ARM64 rebuild because production code was not changed.

findings: Native new-key generation, wrapped key/key-name selection, ONU-ID byte order, sequence/flag/index/fragment fields and AES switch ordering match the shipped ISR for the replayed cases.
The deferred original state machine mainly records protocol state; its absence of direct MMIO is not evidence that the original skips key installation or report transmission.
Original periodic PLOAM watchdog invokes a MAC reset if its TX ready flag remains stuck. This was not copied as a timeout workaround; no hardware cause for a stuck native sender was established.
open_questions: The relationship between changed PON-TAG and a previously installed Class332 MSK remains unresolved at the complete hardware/software lifecycle level. No speculative MSK policy change made.
Replayed key protocol success does not locate the peer business-mapping -110 or explain the approximately50-second O5 restart.
limits: Four deterministic offline key protocol cases only. Tasklet/FSM scheduling, physical interrupts, packet grant timing and optical registration are not tested.
No production driver changes, full test suite, firmware build, device changes, commit or push in this audit.
